question: Which of the following is NOT an allotrope of carbon?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Trisulfur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Trisulfur is a **cherry-red allotrope of sulfur**.
 
• It comprises about **10% of vaporized sulfur at 713 K and 1,333 Pa**.
 
• It is used as an **agrochemical, an antifungal agent, and a Saccharomyces** cerevisiae metabolite.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Diamond:

 
 
• It is a well-known allotrope of carbon.
 
• It exhibits high hardness, high melting point, thermal conductivity, and high dispersion of light.
 
• It is the hardest known natural mineral.
 
• It is widely used in cutting, and jewelry, and as a potential semiconductor material.
 
 
 
• Graphene:
 
 
• It is also an allotrope of carbon
 
• It is a sheet of a single layer of carbon atoms.
 
• Layers of graphene make up graphite.
 
• It is widely used in electronics.
 
 
 
• Fullerene:
 
 
• It is also an allotrope of carbon.
 
• Fullerenes are used in several biomedical applications like carriers of genes etc.
 
 
 
• **Lonsdaleite**:
 
 
• ​It is an allotrope of carbon.
 
• It is also called a hexagonal diamond.
 
• It is found in nature in meteorite debris.
